comment: This review is for his MKT 326 class. He was AMAZING. Super funny and relatable guy. I really enjoyed the discussions and questions he posed for us in class. I would highly recommend him. He does push you and can be a tough grader but he truly wants you to succeed.

Dr. Raggio is passionate about marketing. His lecture is clear and relevant to real life. He is helpful during office hours and will help you learn. Be sure to absorb the lectures because the exam questions require you to understand why something matters. His feedback on the project is great, but the grading criteria are not always clear (no rubric
Randy is so passionate about marketing, however, he tends to ramble on and on. He will absolutely not help your grade.

Dr. Raggio is a good guy and I overall enjoyed his MKT320 Class. He is engaging, relatable, and cares for his students. He is a stickler and has a certain standard to the group work you submit which was a little annoying, but the feedback was still good.

Raggio eats sleeps and breathes bcomm. He is a great professor, very clear spoken and intelligent. I haven't had him for any other class but I bet he's great. However, I find bcomm to be tedius and not always necessary. Nevertheless, he's very kind and funny and will respect you if you try your best.

Dr Raggio is very passionate about the class, especially considering that he taught 6 sessions of the class at a time. It's confusing in the beginning to know what he expects in each assignment, but his feedback was always very thorough. Overall the class wasn't hard, and work was reasonable for a .5 course.

Dr. Raggio was a good professor and very helpful so that his students would master the topics. He instructions are super long and sometimes confusing. Attendance wasn't totally mandatory. The activities pertain to the homework pretty directly which make them important but overall lectures are not the most stimulating. Good class and important.

Best professor I've had so far at UR. He's passionate about what he teaches. Be ready to put efforts in the assignments because he'll make sure you "master" them by making you submit over and over again. His BUAD 205 is manageable and worth it. He's also very caring and understanding :)

One of the most helpful and impactful teachers at UR. Took as a half-credit class and are allowed to resubmit homework until a perfect grade, but work can be slightly hard + time-consuming. Learned some of the most valuable and business lessons and information, and would definitely recommend in first or second semester at UR.

Very arrogant. He's a very nice and helpful guy it just is a lot of work for a half credit class. Writing and presentations are a big part of it and you will have to resubmit work over and over if it's not up to his standards.

Dr. Raggio loves to be an indirect person. He preaches direct writing is necessary for business writing, and yet doesn't practice it. He loves filling up the 1:15 minute BCOMM class with useless information. You are basically guaranteed an A in the class, however, you don't learn anything useful, so that grade is meaningless. Nice guy, bad teacher.
One of the worst classes I have ever taken at Richmond, only a half credit. Not worth it, take Bcomm with somebody else.

Raggio seemed to get a bad rap this semester. He is for sure a harsh grader and doesn't care about hurting your feelings. But this is b/c he truly cares and wants us to be great. All the writing assignments are very doable and the presentations aren't THAT bad (although stressful). It was his first time teaching this course, I'll cut him some slack

Incredibly tough grader. Made me work my ass off to get an B+ in a required half credit course on COMMUNICATION. Kinda ridiculous if you ask me. Grading criteria is not clear at all and it's hard to understand what you aren't doing correctly. Also is rude when leaving comments on writings or presentations. Good luck getting above an A-

Randy is very straight forward 3 exams 1 large marketing project and home work. there is a lot of room to get a good grade and if you pay attention and do all your readings, and put some sort of study effort before exams you will likely get an A- or A

He is the best business professor I have ever had. I would take his class again just because it was that awesome. There's a semester-long group project that was actually really fun. Real life examples and lots of group discussion keep it relevant and engaging.
Raggio was awful. His classes were okay and interesting but tests were hard and his grading was not clear. The group project was huge for an undergrad level.

Very little lecture in his case-intensive class.  Turns the class around and asks questions about cases then has you figure out the answers with his guidance.  Excellent teaching style but a heavy workload.  Easy to skate by for a B but tough to get an A due to some very abstract concepts.
